data.narrative:
Irradiant Technologies, a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Daniel Oran and Amos Meeks, has raised $8.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of nine private firms and one publicly traded peer in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector, including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

The Stage-Progression method represents the sole applicable triangulation approach. Using the $8.5M total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $21M. A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow robotics subsegment; while ten same-sector peers exist, none met the threshold of three datapoints when filtered by stage or valuation tier.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $18M to $24M, centered on $21M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity bounds around the single derived estimate. Key uncertainties include the limited comparable set available at the Seed stage within this specific subsector and reliance on a standard multiplier without adjustment for company-specific unit economics or burn trajectory. Additional visibility into product development milestones and customer traction would refine confidence in this range.
